newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gunmen kidnap high school girls in Algeria, press.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kidnap high school girls in Algeria, press.

text.p: Gunmen, thought to be Moslem guerrillas, have abducted two high school girls on their way to their classes in Medea, 70 km (45 miles) southwest of Algiers, an Algerian newspaper said on Wednesday.
Algeria's main Arab-language Al Khabar said the teenage girls appeared to have been taken to a hideout in Medea, a stronghold for Moslem guerrillas, after their abduction on Tuesday.
Security forces were still searching for the girls, it said.

Separately, troops and police on Tuesday captured bombs and destroyed guerrilla hideouts in a five-hour operation in Djebel Koukou, overlooking Bab el Oued Moslem fundamentalist stronghold in Algiers, said Al Khabar.
The newspaper did not mention casualties.
President Liamine Zeroual on Tuesday told 10 political party leaders that violence was diminishing in Algeria and blamed the latest wave of killings on rival Moslem rebel groups settling scores.

"President Zeroual...appeared very optimistic about the security situation," said one of the 10 officials, speaking to Reuters by telephone from Algiers. The meeting had been called to discuss preparations for parliamentary elections planned for May 29 or June 5.
More than 300 people have died in the past four weeks -- coinciding with the Moslem Ramadan fast -- in massacres and bomb attacks in Algiers and neighbouring hamlets and towns.
The authorities blamed Moslem rebels for the deaths.

About 60,000 people have died in Algeria's violence pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
